references.text: Jesus answers the Pharisees by saying that if the disciples are silent, the stones will cry out. This is a direct continuation of the Pharisees' demand in verse 39, showing that the praise cannot be stopped ([ref:Luk 19:40|Luke 19:40]).

Habakkuk prophesies that the stone shall cry out from the wall – a motif Jesus picks up in his reply to the Pharisees in [ref:Luk 19:40|Luke 19:40], which directly connects to their protest in verse 39 ([ref:Hab 2:11|Habakkuk 2:11]).

The synagogue ruler reacts with indignation when Jesus heals on the Sabbath, just as the Pharisees here try to stop the worship of Jesus. Both events show religious leaders attempting to suppress God's work ([ref:Luk 13:14|Luke 13:14]).

The chief priests and scribes were angry at the children's praise in the temple, and Jesus responded by quoting Psalm 8:3 that God has prepared praise from the mouths of children and infants. The same pattern as in Luke 19:39 – religious leaders protest against the worship of Jesus ([ref:Matt 21:15-16|Matthew 21:15-16]).

The psalm David is quoted by Jesus in Matthew 21:16 in response to similar protests: God has established praise from the mouths of children and infants to silence the enemy. God's praise cannot be silenced ([ref:Sal 8:3|Psalms 8:3]).

The Pharisees and scribes accuse Jesus of blasphemy, asking who can forgive sins except God alone. Their protest in 19:39 is part of the same pattern where the Pharisees oppose Jesus receiving honor that belongs to God ([ref:Luk 5:21|Luke 5:21]).

The Pharisees said to one another, "You see that you are getting nowhere. Look, the whole world has gone after him!" At the entry into Jerusalem, the Pharisees acknowledge their powerlessness against the crowd's enthusiasm, consistent with their attempt in Luke 19:39 to silence the worship ([ref:Joh 12:19|John 12:19]).

After Pentecost, the religious leaders forbid the apostles to speak in Jesus' name, reflecting the same effort made by the Pharisees in Luke 19:39 – to silence the testimony about Jesus ([ref:Apg 4:18|Acts 4:18]).

Gamaliel's advice to the Council: If this is from God, you cannot stop it. This principle highlights the futile attempt by the Pharisees in Luke 19:39 to stop the praise of Jesus ([ref:Apg 5:38-39|Acts 5:38-39]).
